segmentation.text: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a sidewalk
such person shall yield
the right-of-way
to any pedestrian
and shall give audible signal
before overtaking and passing
such pedestrian

elements.justification: The three terms are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle 'a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter 'a device with handlebars and an electric motor ... must not weigh more than one hundred pounds ... maximum speed of not more than twenty miles per hour'), carried as aggregates and never expanded; which classes each includes is the run's reading, and where the reading leaves a class unresolved membership is unknown, which is the rule's faithful verdict, not a defect. 'riding' is read through controlled motion: the device is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt false; its contract 'observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'). 'upon a sidewalk': st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)'); st.sidewalk's exclusion (a crosswalk) does not apply: the words name the sidewalk.

'shall yield' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the subject does not proceed into a conflict; read through the closest-approach primitives, which compute from velocities) and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; rel.contact's exclusion (a near miss) is respected: the near miss is the operationalization's closest-approach bound.
'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'); same mapping as the index's 'to any pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: preference over another approaching 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the moving subject's centre within the conflict horizon is approaching so as to give rise to the danger of a crash

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (membership of the three admitted aggregates, as the run's reading classifies them) that occupies an st.sidewalk region (rel.occupies) and is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance)).
obligation: For every pedestrian p of the scene other than the subject (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A scene with no pedestrian is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'any person is riding' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the sidewalk is read as ridden.
Yielding is read as not proceeding into a conflict and not colliding: while riding, the subject keeps every pedestrian outside the conflict bound.

param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

segmentation.text: The parking of vehicles is prohibited or restricted in certain zones as set forth in this Section.

The location of such zones shall be established by posting appropriate signage or other durable markings, by painting curbs or the edges of road surfaces in accordance with the colors listed below, or by a combination thereof:
Red indicates no stopping, standing or parking,
whether or not the vehicle is attended and whether or not the engine or motor is running,
subject to the following:
(1) Except as provided in this Subsection,
a curb or road surface edge which is painted red indicates no parking,
whether or not accompanied by signage to that effect.
(2) When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos,
those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes for the loading or unloading of passengers. (3)
When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited to RTC buses,
those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes for the loading or unloading of passengers. (4)
Armored cars and emergency vehicles may park at such locations
for the period necessary to conduct their business,
whether or not there is accompanying signage so indicating.
(5) At locations where a drop box for U.S. mail is adjacent to a curb or road surface painted red,
a person may stop
for the period of time necessary to expeditiously deposit mail in such a drop box.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), one atom, never expanded; the zones the sentence introduces are read by the spans that state them.

The zones are established by signage, durable markings or painted curbs and road-surface edges: st.curb_zone 'a signed or marked length of curb; kind ...; colour in {red, yellow, white, blue, gray, none} where the curb itself is painted' is such a zone, its presence the evidence that it is established (observable_reading status); rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)' anchors the subject in the zone, so no other zone of the scene is read.

'Red': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.curb_zone whose colour is red. 'no stopping': 'stopping' is DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation') at any duration; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts too, so their purpose exclusions add nothing once every halt is barred. The definition's exclusion the concept does not make is carried beside it in the obligation, so that a halt it excludes is no prohibited stop and the duty is met: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' - another road user ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within a queue gap of the bodies (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not centre distance); 'or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' - a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal showing a red indication (circular_red, red_arrow(dir), flashing_red), or a dev.stop_sign, governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies. dev.governs is not a position, and none is read from it.

'a curb or road surface edge which is painted red': st.curb_zone with colour red ('colour ... where the curb itself is painted'), the subject anchored by rel.occupies. The no-parking it restates is contained in the no-stopping of s3, so it adds no second duty.

Nearest atoms only; the span carries gap (s9). 'signage which indicates that parking is limited to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos': the red zone the subject occupies is of st.curb_zone kind tour_bus_loading ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind in {..., tour_bus_loading, ...}'), its signage the evidence (observable_reading status). 'tour buses, shuttle buses and limos' are the admitted aggregates DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus, DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::shuttle_bus and DEF-LVMC-11-02-090::limo, each one atom, never replaced by ru.tour_bus_or_limousine. The run's reading includes no class under these ids: ru.tour_bus_or_limousine joins tour and shuttle buses with limousines, so it is unresolved under each, and membership is never decided for any vehicle; the exception's membership leaf is then vacuous, which the gap states.

'those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes': the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) and the time since it came to rest in the zone (sinceRise of drv.motion.complete_halt and rel.occupies of the zone) is at most the literal thirty minutes: the period is that of the current halt. 'for the loading or unloading of passengers' is a purpose read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).

'signage which indicates that parking is limited to RTC buses': the red zone is of st.curb_zone kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind in {..., bus_stop, ...}'), the length of curb signed for buses, its signage the evidence (observable_reading status). 'RTC buses' is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-120::rtc_bus, one atom, never replaced by ru.transit_bus.
Same as s10: the subject is at rest and the time since it came to rest in the zone is at most the literal thirty minutes; the passenger purpose is read through the halt (observable_reading purpose).

'Armored cars': ru.official_vehicle with kind armored_car ('kind in {..., armored_car, ...}'); its exclusion (an emergency vehicle) is respected, the emergency vehicle being its own atom. 'emergency vehicles': ru.emergency_vehicle ('vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency'), the class the words name, not a responding vehicle, so the 'responding' exclusion does not apply. 'may park at such locations': their halt (drv.motion.complete_halt) in the red zone.

'for the period necessary to conduct their business': a purpose, read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose): the armored car's or emergency vehicle's halt in the zone, whatever its length.

'a drop box for U.S. mail': st.obstruction kind mail_drop_box ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind in {..., mail_drop_box, ...}'). 'At locations where [it] is adjacent to a curb ... painted red': the subject, in the red zone, has its body within a reach of the drop box (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); a reach relating the box to the road user, not a relation between two regions; geometry is not used for occupancy.

'a person may stop': the vehicle's halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation'), the person read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). 'stop' is a halting under both posted definitions.

operationalizations.standard: for the period of time necessary to expeditiously deposit mail in such a drop box
operationalizations.convention: curbside dwell of a single drop-off: the time to pull up, reach the box from the vehicle or a step away and post the mail; the halt counts as expeditious while the subject is at rest and the time since it came to rest in the zone (sinceRise of drv.motion.complete_halt and rel.occupies) is at most the parameter

residues.why: 'whether or not the vehicle is attended and whether or not the engine or motor is running' makes the duty the same in every case: the halt is barred either way, so neither occupancy nor kin.engine_running is read.
'whether or not accompanied by signage to that effect': the red paint alone marks the zone; a sign beside it changes nothing.
'whether or not there is accompanying signage so indicating': the armored car and emergency vehicle exception holds with or without a sign.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation bind a region z of kind st.curb_zone whose colour is red, with rel.occupies(subject, z). Exceptions (the duty does not apply): (2) the subject is a tour bus, shuttle bus or limo (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus, DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::shuttle_bus or DEF-LVMC-11-02-090::limo), z is of kind tour_bus_loading, the subject is at rest (drv_motion_complete_halt(subject), speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance), and Term.sinceRise(drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) and rel.occupies(subject, z)) is at most the literal thirty minutes; (3) the subject is an RTC bus (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-120::rtc_bus), z is of kind bus_stop, the subject is at rest, and the same time is at most the literal thirty minutes; (4) the subject is a ru.official_vehicle of kind armored_car or a ru.emergency_vehicle; (5) some st.obstruction o of kind mail_drop_box has st_region_geometry_distance(subject, o) at most p.mail_drop_box_reach, the subject is at rest, and the time since the subject came to rest in z is at most p.mail_deposit_max_halt. Each halt-duration test is unknown where the halt began before the recording; an aggregate membership the reading leaves unresolved leaves its exception unknown wherever it decides it.
obligation: The subject does not stop in z otherwise than as the definition of stopping excludes: drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) implies (some road user u, not the subject, with rel.ahead_behind_in_lane(u ahead of subject) and rel_surface_gap(subject, u) at most p.queue_halt_gap) or (some device governing a travel region the subject occupies directs a halt: a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, red_arrow(dir) or flashing_red, or a dev.stop_sign). A halt the definition excludes is no prohibited stop: the duty applies to it and is met.

narrowings.why: The zones' establishment by sign, marking or paint is read through the signed or marked curb zone's presence.

'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' in the definition of stopping is read as a halt with another road user ahead in the subject's lane within the queue gap; a conflict that does not show as a road user ahead in the lane is not read. The officer's or device's direction is read as a stop indication, a red signal indication or a stop sign governing the subject's travel region.
Signage limiting parking to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos is read through the curb zone's kind tour_bus_loading.
'for the loading or unloading of passengers' is read through the halt it explains; whether passengers board is not read.
Signage limiting parking to RTC buses is read through the curb zone's kind bus_stop.
'for the loading or unloading of passengers' is read through the halt it explains.
'the period necessary to conduct their business' is read as the armored car's or emergency vehicle's halt itself, at any length; the business is not observable.
'a person may stop' is read through the vehicle's halt.
'to deposit mail' is read through a halt beside the drop box within the bound; whether mail is deposited is not read.

segmentation.text: The parking of vehicles is prohibited or restricted in certain zones as set forth in this Section.

The location of such zones shall be established by posting appropriate signage or other durable markings, by painting curbs or the edges of road surfaces in accordance with the colors listed below, or by a combination thereof:
Yellow indicates a zone for:
(1) Commercial vehicles to stop, stand or park for the purpose of loading or unloading freight
in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign; and
(2) Taxicabs to stop, stand, park for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers
in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), one atom, never expanded; 'is prohibited or restricted in certain zones' introduces the restriction the yellow zone states.

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_52_030_A: st.curb_zone 'a signed or marked length of curb; ... colour ... where the curb itself is painted', whose presence is the evidence that the zone was established (observable_reading status); rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)') anchors the subject in it.

'Yellow indicates a zone for' the uses listed: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.curb_zone of colour yellow. Because the zone is for those uses only, any other halt in it (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation') is restricted. 'stop' in the list has two posted definitions (DEF-NRS-484A-255, DEF-NRS-484A-260), each with its own scope. Both are a halting, and the halting is what the concept reads, so neither is chosen over the other.

Nearest atoms only; the span carries gap (s4). 'Commercial vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle ('a motor vehicle or combination of motor vehicle and trailer maintained or used primarily for the furtherance of a commercial enterprise'), one atom, never replaced by ru.commercial_motor_vehicle or ru.truck, which the definition's words do not equate with it. The run's reading includes no class under it, so membership is never decided and the exception's leaf is vacuous, which the gap states. 'to stop, stand or park': its halt (drv.motion.complete_halt). 'for the purpose of loading or unloading freight' is a purpose, read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).

'an accompanying sign' is a dev.zone_sign of kind parking_restricted ('a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; ... conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend - a list of time windows ..., a duration limit, a vehicle class'). It governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the lane beside the curb. 'in accordance with the conditions and times posted' is prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user') for the subject. The dev.zone_sign contract does not state whether the condition holds now (its exclusion); the primitive does.

Nearest atoms only; the span carries gap (s6). 'Taxicabs' is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab ('a motor vehicle which is properly licensed under State and local law to provide taxicab service for a charge or fee'), one atom, never replaced by ru.taxicab. The run's reading includes no class under it (ru.taxicab is unresolved), so membership is never decided, which the gap states. 'to stop, stand, park': its halt (drv.motion.complete_halt). 'for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers' is read through the halt it explains (observable_reading purpose).

Same words, same atoms as s5: a dev.zone_sign of kind parking_restricted governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.conditions_hold for the subject.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation, some region z of kind st.curb_zone whose colour is yellow has rel.occupies(subject, z). The duty does not apply under either exception. (1) The subject is a commercial vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-070::commercial_vehicle), and some dev.zone_sign d of kind parking_restricted governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.conditions_hold(d, subject). (2) The subject is a taxicab (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab), and such a sign's conditions hold for it. Each exception is a conjunction of the membership and the sign's conditions. Where the conditions are decided not to hold, the exception is false whatever the membership. Where they hold and membership is unknown under the run's reading, the exception is unknown.
obligation: The subject does not halt in z: not drv_motion_complete_halt(subject), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, judged at the observations where the applicability holds, so the halt judged is a halt in the yellow zone.

narrowings.why: The zones' establishment by sign, marking or paint is read through the presence of the signed or marked curb zone.

'a zone for' commercial vehicles and taxicabs is read as barring the halt of any other vehicle in the yellow zone. It also bars their own halt where the accompanying sign's conditions do not hold. A halt outside the sign's hours is read as outside the conditions posted.
'for the purpose of loading or unloading freight' is read through the commercial vehicle's halt; whether freight moves is not read.
The accompanying sign is read as a parking_restricted zone sign governing the lane beside the curb that the subject occupies. Its posting is the evidence of its force.
'for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for passengers' is read through the taxicab's halt.
The accompanying sign is read as a parking_restricted zone sign governing the lane beside the curb that the subject occupies.

no person shall park
any vehicle
on any street
for a period of time longer than thirty minutes
between the hours of one a.m. and six a.m. of any day.

elements.justification: Nearest atoms only; the span carries gap (s1). 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The class atom ru.motor_vehicle never replaces an admitted aggregate. A trailer drawn by another vehicle is not 'self-propelled', so the definition's words leave it out; but the only class that carries a trailer, ru.trailer_or_combination, also carries the combination with its self-propelled towing vehicle, so the run's reading leaves it unresolved, and no vehicle is ever decided not to be a motor vehicle: the duty is never decided, which the gap states.

'park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading'; drv.motion.parked denotes 'at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration', a shorter halt 'is not denoted'. Same mapping as the index's 'it is unlawful to park'.
'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Street' applies DEF-NRS-484A-265 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' (not the roadway alone; its exclusion does not apply since the definition takes the entire width). rel.occupies anchors the vehicle's footprint on it. The city limits are the jurisdiction this city ordinance applies in.

'for a period of time longer than thirty minutes' is one continuous period of parking, a time window behind the observation of the stated length at every observation of which the vehicle was parked on the street within the hours; the window reads kin.time, 'instant of observation of a scene'.

env.civil_time is 'the local calendar time of the observation: date, weekday, time of day (from the recording's metadata, not from the scene)'; its time of day is read as the minute of the day, a count (unit 1), so the stated hours are declared in that count: one a.m. is minute 60 of the day and six a.m. minute 360, compared directly with the field with no conversion factor. 'Not a stand-in for: kin.time' does not apply: the clock of day, not the order of observations, is read.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and not a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle does not hold), its footprint overlaps a street (st.highway, rel.occupies), and the civil minute of the day (env.civil_time) is at or after minute 60 (one a.m.) and before minute 360 (six a.m.).
obligation: It is not the case that, at every observation of the time window of thirty minutes behind the observation, the subject was parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration) with its footprint on a street and with the civil minute of the day at or after minute 60 (one a.m.) and before minute 360 (six a.m.).

narrowings.why: 'no person shall park' is read through the vehicle's own standing, whoever controls it; the definition's temporary halt for loading or unloading is read through the halt's duration (min_duration), the purpose itself not being observed.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsections 3 and 4,
a driver
shall not drive on the left side of the highway within such zone or drive across or on the left side of any pavement striping designed to mark such zone throughout its length.
A driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such zone
to an adjoining highway if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
and there will be no impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.
Except where otherwise provided,
a driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such a zone
to make a left-hand turn
if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
in compliance with NRS 484B.413 [NRS-484B-413-2],
if it is safe
and if it would not be an impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.

elements.justification: DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'driver' means 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'. The driver is a relational role, not membership (ru.aggregate: 'Not a stand-in for: a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle'), so the role is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle (observable_reading agency) and the binder is the vehicle, 'true when the user carries an included class' of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the same mapping the index records for 'a driver'.

(i) The left side of the highway is the side to the left of the line dividing its two directions: st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the highway the subject occupies by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'; we read the way, not the roadway, so its exclusion does not apply). Being on the left side is read with prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', against half the body's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'): the body is on the left side where the line's offset is below half the width by more than p.lateral_position_tolerance. (ii) 'Such zone' is the no-passing zone the section's first subsection lets an authority indicate 'by appropriate signs or markings'. A sign: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind in {..., no_passing, ...}; end attribute', with dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', on a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the sign read is a beginning sign (end false); its 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' does not apply since no legend condition is read. A marking: st.lane_marking, 'per side of a lane: type in {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour in {white, yellow, other}', on the left side of the st.lane the subject occupies: a solid or double_solid yellow line marks the zone for that lane; a solid_broken line, whose solid half the atom does not place, leaves membership unknown. The zone's presence on the road is the evidence of its designation (status). (iii) The pavement striping designed to mark the zone is that no-passing marking (st.lane_marking type solid or double_solid, colour yellow, on the left side of the subject's lane), which on a two-way highway lies along st.centre_line. Driving across it or on its left side is the body reaching past that line: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line ('left positive') below half the width from kin.extent less p.lateral_position_tolerance. 'Throughout its length' is read by judging every observation at which the subject is in the zone.

The permitted act is the same crossing the obligation forbids: the vehicle's body reaching past the zone's centre-line striping, prim.region_lateral_offset ('left positive') against half the kin.extent width; 'A driver' is the vehicle, as in s2.

'To an adjoining highway' states where the crossing leads, a purpose read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') other than the highway h of the zone and no longer occupies h. 'Has first given the appropriate turn signal': sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}', showing left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {..., left, ...}', meaning left, at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since). The indicator's 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' does not apply: the signal is read, not the manoeuvre.

The same crossing as s6 (prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line against half the kin.extent width) by the vehicle. The region at which the left-hand turn of s11 is declared is the place a left turn leaves the highway for: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'); the declared intention takes one of them as its target.

'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'. Oncoming: rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos; its exclusion (not the direction a road user approaches an intersection from) does not apply, as the words concern road users meeting the subject head-on on this highway. Following: a member behind the subject, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for ... immediately to the rear)' (rel.bearing, negative longitudinal component), with 'headings aligned' (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.contest_same_direction_cos).

As s8b: members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that are oncoming (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing') or following (behind by rel.bearing, 'immediately to the rear', with rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

The appropriate signal for a crossing to the left to make a left-hand turn is sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'), given at the last observation before the crossing began; its manner and distance are the compliance with NRS 484B.413 composed on s13. Not the turn itself (indicator's exclusion).

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a road user of traffic is impeded where its centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; oncoming is rel.oncoming within the opposed-heading tolerance, following is a road user behind the subject (negative longitudinal bearing) with headings aligned within the same-direction tolerance; read at every observation of the crossing

traffic-conflict technique: the crossing is safe where no road user of the scene is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; read at every observation of the crossing

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: as for s8: traffic-conflict technique on oncoming (rel.oncoming) and following (behind, headings aligned) members of traffic, read at every observation of the crossing

residues.why: 'Except where otherwise provided' defers to provisions it does not name; those provisions are judged by their own rules, and this rule's verdict on crossing the striping to make a left-hand turn is the same whether or not they apply.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a highway h on which a centre line c lies, and is within a no-passing zone: it occupies a travel region that a dev.zone_sign of kind no_passing (end false) governs, or it occupies a lane whose left-side st.lane_marking is solid or double_solid and yellow (where that marking is solid_broken, membership is unknown).
obligation: At every such observation the subject's body does not reach past the centre line c to its left: the lateral offset of c from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, left positive) is not below half the subject's width (kin.extent) minus p.lateral_position_tolerance. A crossing is excused (E3) where, within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead, the subject occupies a highway other than h and no longer occupies h; at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since) its turn indicator showed left or its hand signal meant left; and at every observation of the crossing no member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is oncoming (rel.oncoming, p.oncoming_heading_cos) or following (behind by rel.bearing, rel.same_direction within p.contest_same_direction_cos) has a closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A crossing is also excused (E4) where the subject's declared intention int.left_turn at an intersection or a driveway/alley entrance holds at the observation; the left signal was given as in E3; NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with for the subject; no road user is in contact with the subject or has such a closest approach (safe); and no oncoming or following member of traffic has such a closest approach (impediment).

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

The striping designed to mark the zone is read where it lies along the centre line dividing the two directions; a no-passing marking between two lanes of the same direction is not read as the zone's striping.
'to an adjoining highway' is read through the conduct it explains: the subject reaching another highway within the turn window after the crossing
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic; a slowing of traffic without such a conflict is not read

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield
and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which the subject is a member; 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic') governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.
A dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), read at the subject's entry.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.complete_halt); 'in obedience to a stop sign' ties the halt to a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X. 'Yield in compliance with a yield sign' (dev.yield_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'), in the manner subsection 1 prescribes ('in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped'), is the subject's kin.speed within the place's stopping zone at or below the speed from which it still halts at the place (p.yield_line_speed_max), a halt included. The act is owed at the place that manner names, which the act's own atoms read: the st.stop_line marking c (st.entrance_of), else the st.crosswalk marking c, else c's entrance end, the side along c's direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along, the body-to-mark distance by st.region_geometry, the subject on c by rel.occupies.

'Prior to entering an intersection': the act is owed before the subject's entry into X - the observation at which its footprint comes to overlap X (rel.occupies), having occupied at the previous observation a carrier c entering X (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region).

'A stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto': a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs (dev.governs) an approach carrier of X (st.lane_enters) or X; the sign the subject obeys is the one governing its own entrance c, which it occupies (rel.occupies).

residues.why: 'although' is concessive: the duty reaches signed entrances whether or not the intersection is part of a through highway, and the stop or yield owed at a signed entrance is the same in both cases (subsection 1 states the same act where it is part of one); the words withhold the duty nowhere.

applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); where at the entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governs c or X (dev.governs); except where at that observation a police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governs c or X, or a traffic signal that is not inoperative governs c or X.
obligation: NRS_484B_257_1_o1 (binder subject to subject) is complied with at the entry - the manner subsection 1 prescribes - and the act it states is found on the approach: where a stop sign governs c or X, a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign does, an observation at which kin.speed is at or below p.yield_line_speed_max (a halt included); in either case while occupying c within the stopping zone of the place for c, in subsection 1's order: (1) a stop line marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), the line ahead of or at the reference point along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero), the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (2) where no stop line marks c (entrance lists observed and excluding c), the crosswalk marking c's entrance ahead, not overlapped, the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, the footprint outside X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start - the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction and farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) - or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever is later. Act found: compliant; either end reached without it: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own act; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs c, but an operating dev.traffic_signal (circular_red) also governs c at the subject's entry.

segmentation.text: Upon approaching
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency
which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Decrease the speed of his or her vehicle
to a speed that is reasonable and proper, pursuant to the criteria set forth in subsection 1 of NRS 484B.600 [NRS-484B-600-1a].

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'approaching' the emergency vehicle: the subject moves (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance) with the emergency vehicle ahead of it in its own frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive), within the centre distance (rel.centre_distance 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') at which its lamps engage the approaching driver. rel.centre_distance's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival') is respected: it only bounds the range of the approach.

Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; its conduct is carried by t4 and t6.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

'moving': the emergency vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'preparing to move', as t12 defines it, 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver ... including ... (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver': sig.hand_signal 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}' with a meaning other than no_signal, or sig.turn_indicator 'state in {off, left, right}' other than off (a further visible indication of the open list; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' respected: it is read as the indication, not the move), with the emergency vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight').

Nearest atom only; the span carries gap (t6). sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...' denotes the lamp, and the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front' needs colour red, mode flashing and facing front; the formula surface reads the atom only by colour and mode, so a lit red flashing lamp of any facing is all a rule can state, a weaker condition than the words; not a stand-in for an audible warning.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation,
the driver of a vehicle
shall yield the right-of-way,
slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk
when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning,
or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger.

As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

elements.justification: The official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that regulate a crosswalk crossing are the vehicular signal heads (dev.traffic_signal, state including 'dark') and pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal, state including 'dark') that control the travel regions the vehicle and the pedestrian are in: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), with rel.occupies anchoring each road user in a governed region (kind st.travel_region). 'not in operation' is a head showing 'dark' or dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'); 'not in place' is no such head governing those regions. dev.governs is used for control, not for a position, as its exclusion requires.

'the driver of a vehicle' maps, as in the run's index, to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions decided by the reading); 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian: no rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard below sets; as mapped in the run's index for 'shall yield the right-of-way'.

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'crossing the highway within a crosswalk': the crosswalk (DEF-NRS-484A-065: 'That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing') is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), marked or unmarked, so the definition's whole extent is kept; rel.occupies places the pedestrian's footprint in it.

By the section's own definition, a half of the highway is 'all traffic lanes ... designated for traffic traveling in one direction': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) or a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') points with the vehicle's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'): the half on which the vehicle travels, or, while it turns, the half its heading has turned onto. kin.heading is read as the direction of travel of a vehicle driven forward; st.lane 'Not a stand-in for' a half of the roadway does not apply because the half is assembled from the lanes' designated directions, as the definition itself builds it.

The section's definition of 'half of the highway' ('all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction', 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') is carried by the lanes (st.lane) grouped by their designated direction (st.lane_direction) and by a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the atoms c3 and st2 read.

operationalizations.standard: slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield (the right-of-way's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash the driver has not yielded to; a vehicle at rest has slowed or stopped as need be

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian in the crosswalk on a lane whose designated direction points against the vehicle's heading is in danger where the predicted closest approach of the two centres falls within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. Devices are not in place or not in operation: every traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies shows dark or is inoperative (dev.inoperative). There is a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), such that every pedestrian signal head governing a travel region p occupies shows dark, p is not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B, and either (a) p's footprint overlaps a lane or one-way roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) has a positive dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) — the subject's half — or (b) otherwise (p on the opposite half) the predicted closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'official' is read through the presence of the signal heads in the scene.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle
which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').

Leaving 'a curb or other place of safety' is the pedestrian's footprint (rel.occupies) coming onto the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') from a place pedestrians are safe from vehicles: the sidewalk the curb bounds (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'), a safety zone (st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only') or a median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider). st.sidewalk is not used for a crosswalk, as its exclusion requires; st.roadway is not used for the sidewalk. 'into the path of a vehicle': the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the pedestrian is in its path where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). These primitives are 'Not a stand-in for' contact or danger alone; here they bound the path the vehicle will sweep, the clearance and horizon set by the reading, and the impossibility is decided by the standard.

operationalizations.standard: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the vehicle cannot yield where the time to the predicted closest approach (prim.closest_approach_time) is less than the driver's perception-reaction time plus the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) divided by twice the braking deceleration, written as a product (2·a·t_ca < 2·a·t_r + v); the deceleration is selected by the surface: icy or snow-covered (env.ice_or_snow), else wet (env.wet_road), else dry

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that leaves a place of safety at this observation: its footprint overlaps a roadway (st.roadway) here, and at the previous observation it overlapped no roadway and overlapped a sidewalk, a safety zone or a median or divider. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject, nor where LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 is engaged for a vehicle v of the scene.
obligation: There is no vehicle v (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) such that the closest approach of the subject and v falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) and 2·a·t < 2·a·p.driver_reaction_time + speed(v), where t is prim.closest_approach_time with horizon p.conflict_horizon, speed(v) is v's kin.speed, and a is p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road holds, else p.following_decel_dry. With no vehicle in the scene, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'suddenly' is read through the vehicle's closeness at the moment the pedestrian leaves the place of safety: a departure is sudden in the law's sense where the vehicle is already too close to yield; the pedestrian's own abruptness is not measured.
'other place of safety' is read only through the sidewalk the curb bounds, a safety zone and a median or dividing section.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's motion: whether the vehicle can stop, whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated,
pedestrians facing the signal
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
and must be given
the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}'); 'in place' is a head present in the scene. 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'), traffic including pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles'), ties the head to the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (kinds st.roadway, st.lane). dev.governs is not used as a position.
'the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated' is the head's state walk (dev.pedestrian_signal state 'walk').

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'facing the signal': the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along the direction its body points (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'), within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as the place of a stop line or crossing, which its exclusion names.

'may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' identifies the pedestrians the right-of-way is owed to: those on the roadway the head governs (rel.occupies of a st.roadway or st.lane region that head governs), facing the head, so moving toward it across the way. The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines') is crossed by traversing its roadway; the sidewalk the words of the sibling subparagraphs call a place of safety is no part of the crossing.

Giving the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian (no rel.contact) with its speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard sets, as the index maps 'Yield'.
'the drivers of all vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash in which the vehicle has not granted precedence

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), a pedestrian signal head d showing walk, and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), with p's footprint overlapping r (rel.occupies), p facing d, and p not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B. p faces d where, with Δ the vector from p's kin.position to d's dev.position and h p's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach².
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion: the duty binds each vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal,
but must complete the crossing before the countdown timer gets to zero.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'); 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control, read through dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'; traffic includes pedestrians, DEF-NRS-484A-285) on a roadway or lane (kinds st.roadway, st.lane).

'“Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The pedestrian who proceeds across the highway under this indication is one whose footprint came onto the governed roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) while the head showed it, facing the head: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach — the direction of the signal. dev.position is not used as a crossing or a stop line.

Completing the crossing is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps it (rel.occupies). The countdown timer gets to zero at the end of the flashing interval it times, where the head stops showing the flashing indication with a countdown and shows dont_walk_steady (dev.pedestrian_signal states dont_walk_flashing with countdown, then dont_walk_steady).

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the countdown's end for a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest entry onto r (the latest earlier observation at which its footprint came to overlap r, not overlapping it at the observation before; history bound: that entry, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown and the subject faced d, and d showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown at every observation from that entry to the previous one. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where the entry lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: At the countdown's end the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has completed the crossing.

narrowings.why: the countdown's reaching zero is read as the head's change from the flashing indication with countdown to the steady indication, which ends the interval the timer counts; the timer's displayed number is not read.
'complete the crossing' is read as the pedestrian's footprint having left the roadway or lane governed by the head; a pedestrian on a median or safety zone between roadways has left it.

scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian entered r while the head showed walk; at the countdown's end it is still on r (the steady-indication duty governs it, not this one).

scenarios.name: blind

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian ('such signals') is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The head s is the one governing the rider's approach carrier (s7). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' requires the halt itself (rule 5), with every qualification of the requirement it names, borrowed from NRS-484B-307-8a (reference s3): 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A stop required is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement': drv.motion.complete_halt. The place: the stop line (st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') recorded as marking the entrance of the rider's carrier c (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at the intersection (st.intersection); the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance), on the approach that ends in this entry, as NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states the place, zone and history bound. The admitted aggregates for the defined words: DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'), DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'), DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion (narrowing). Membership is decided by the run's reading of these definitions: where it leaves a class unresolved under one of them (as it does ru.motor_vehicle), a road user of that class is of unknown membership, and the rule reports unknown for it rather than not_applicable.

'may proceed straight through or turn right or left': the rider's entry into intersection i (st.intersection), its footprint coming to overlap i (rel.occupies) having occupied at the observation before a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); every movement through i is admitted. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'the applicable official traffic-control device': the signal installation of the intersection the rider is at, observed through its heads: the traffic signal heads (dev.traffic_signal) that govern (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection); the head s governing c is the rider's own. 'official' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'placed or erected by a public authority') is presumed from the head's presence (narrowing). 'waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows': from the latest onset of its halt at the place until its entry into i the rider does not overlap i, and in that interval some head of the installation begins a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow, the lights or lighted arrows that come on once in each cycle of the installation) at least two times: a count of that head's rising green indications since the halt's onset, against the literal two. These are the nearest atoms only: the count's bound, the figure two the law states, cannot be written as a literal the formula carries (gap on this span).
'the signal does not change': the rider's head s (dev.traffic_signal) displays the steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation from the latest onset of the halt to the entry.

'No other device at the place prohibits': a regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', codes no_left_turn and no_right_turn) governing (dev.governs) the rider's carrier c (st.travel_region) or the intersection i (st.intersection). Not a stand-in: 'a prohibition sign is a condition', and it is read as one, not as a manoeuvre. 'official' status is presumed from presence.

'either or both such turns, if applicable': the turn the rider makes on this passage through intersection i (st.intersection), from its entry (rel.occupies rising) to its exit, recognized at the exit as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region, 'a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r') or a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region); 'if applicable': only a turn made brings a prohibition into play, and a straight passage is never prohibited by a turn sign. Read from each observation of the passage at the recognition the passage reaches, so that the condition is decided at the entry where the exit is recorded.

'yields': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a rider that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s14 reads. As the index maps 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians and other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian and DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the rider. 'proceeding': moving, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'as directed by the signal at the intersection': it overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a travel region that enters i (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), or it occupies a travel region c' entering i that is governed (dev.governs) by a head displaying a green indication (dev.traffic_signal: circular_green or green_arrow). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the rider grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

compositions.quote: must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection
compositions.why: The words borrow the requirement's place and its order (the crosswalk on the nearest side, or the place a sign or pavement marking indicates, else the intersection's edge) and the meaning of stopping before it. The condition requires that the halt itself occurred there; a composition with NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 would not establish it, since a composed rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged, and this paragraph governs riders whether or not that duty engages them (a bicycle or electric scooter is no vehicle). So the borrowed words are carried by the halt, the place and the approach on s2, and no rule of NRS-484B-307-8a need apply, hold or be complied with.

residues.why: The words give the cause of the unchanged red. A head that keeps its steady red alone through two complete cycles of the installation's other indications while the rider waits at its stop place has not served the rider's approach, which is a malfunction or a failure to detect the rider; the duty is the same whichever of the two causes holds, and neither shows in the scene beyond the unchanged red (s8) and the cycles (s7), which the rule reads.

applicability: The subject is of one of the classes motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (admitted aggregates) or a ru.motorcycle (the trimobile). It approached intersection i through a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs), and halted (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the place of the stop on that approach: the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance, else the crosswalk recorded as marking it, else c's entrance end at i, with the zone (p.stop_point_tolerance) and the history bound NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states. From the latest onset of that halt until its entry into i, s displayed a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at every observation and the subject's footprint did not overlap i; in that interval some traffic signal head governing a travel region that enters i began a green indication (circular_green or a green_arrow rising) at least two times (literal 2). The subject then entered i (its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c at the observation before) while s still displayed the steady red alone, and its footprint has overlapped i at every observation since that entry, the judged one included. It is not the case that the passage through i begun at that entry is recognized at its exit (at the judged observation or a later one: the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap i) as a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region; step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min) while a regulatory sign coded no_right_turn governs c or i, nor as a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region) while one coded no_left_turn governs c or i; where no such sign governs, this condition holds whatever the movement, and where one governs and the exit is not recorded, it is unknown.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian or of the class traffic and is proceeding as directed by the signal at i — its speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and either its footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i, or it occupies a travel region c' entering i governed by a head that displays circular_green or a green_arrow: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at its controls.
'official' traffic-control device: the presence of the signal heads at the intersection is the evidence of their official status.

'proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection' is read through the signal state governing the other road user's approach (a green indication) where it approaches, and through its presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk where it is there; a road user that entered against its own red and is now within the intersection is yielded to as well.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moped halts 1 m short of the stop line marking lane c's entrance while head s displays circular_red alone; while it waits, the head governing the cross street's lane begins circular_green twice and s stays circular_red alone; no turn-prohibiting sign governs c or i. The moped enters i straight through at 5 m/s while a pedestrian walks at 1.3 m/s in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the far approach, the closest approach of their centres 1.0 s ahead at 0.6 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same wait and entry with no other road user in the scene: the duty binds the rider alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The moped halts at the line and enters i after the cross street's head has begun circular_green only once since its halt: the wait of two cycles is not met.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the heads govern: which head is the rider's and whether the cross head belongs to this intersection are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the moped halted 15 m short of the line behind a queue and, when the queue cleared, rolled to the line and into i without halting at the place: the halt the requirement to stop names did not occur, and the paragraph does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a regulatory sign coded no_right_turn governs lane c and the moped's passage through i is recognized at its exit as a right turn (heading change -85 degrees): a device at the place prohibits the turn it made, and the permission with its yield does not arise.

param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_20_060_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
