gaps.proposal: `Formula.countAtLeast` (edge : Formula) (sinceφ : Formula) (n : Term): the count of rising edges of `edge` since `sinceφ` became true (start of its latest run) is at least `n`, where `n` is a constant term in unit count (a Term.lit written through the count unit), so that Formula.literals reports the bound as (n, count) and the gate's literal check reads the figure the law states. Alternatively, Formula.count keeps its form and Formula.literals and the gate's literal collection report its Nat bound as (n, count). It decides the time of the act the law requires before a rider may proceed against a steady red: the wait of two complete cycles of the installation's lights, which separates a lawful proceed after a detector failure from running the red after one cycle. Same distinction as gap G87 filed on NRS-484B-307-9b.
gaps.nearest: Formula.count (edge sinceφ op n) writes the count of the installation's rising green indications since the halt's onset, but its bound n is a bare Nat that Formula.literals does not report: a faithful rule shows formula literals [] against the declared literal (2, count) and the gate returns it BARE_LITERAL. Adding a tautological Term.lit 2 count conjunct, or dropping the figure the law states from the record's literals, is forbidden.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal

must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection,
and,
except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) [(c) is appended below, NRS-484B-307-8d],
must remain stopped or standing until the green signal is shown.
After complying with the requirement to stop,
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a right turn
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a left turn
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'remain stopped or standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle ... otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers') at the place of the stop: the subject's footprint does not come to overlap (rel.occupies) the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.crosswalk, st.entrance_of) nor intersection i (st.intersection). 'until the green signal is shown': the duty holds while the head (dev.traffic_signal) displays the steady red alone and ends once it displays another state. Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' refers to s3 of this line and requires the halt itself with every qualification s3 states: 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt; DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement') at that place — the stop line (st.stop_line) recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at i (st.intersection) — with the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry), on the approach that ends in this entry: the place, zone and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1. The halt itself, not compliance with that node, which a composed rule grants where it is not engaged. In this node the condition is read where the permission of paragraph (c) takes the subject out of the duty to remain stopped.

'vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'facing such a signal': the steady red head governs (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters). 'situated on the extreme right of the highway': c is a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'): the rightmost lane. Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from a lateral offset.

'may proceed into the intersection': the subject proceeding from the travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) toward and into i, its footprint leaving the place of the stop (rel.occupies of the crosswalk marking c's entrance or of i rising); the place at which the intention of s10 is declared. As the index maps 'may proceed into the intersection' (NRS_484B_307_8a_o3).

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') that i lies on (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') other than a highway c lies on. 'two-directional' (DEF-NRS-484B-073, 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'): no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on it, and two lanes (st.lane) lying on it carry designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose cosine is below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'one-way to the right': at least one lane lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction to the right of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's (d_x times l_y minus d_y times l_x) being below minus p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is the way a region lies on, not nearness; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier.

'vehicular traffic facing such a signal': as s8. 'situated on the extreme left': c is a lane (st.lane) of ordinal 1 (st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'); 'of a one-way highway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), as the index maps 'Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic' (NRS_484B_220_1). Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from an offset.
As s9: the subject proceeding from c into i (rel.occupies rising; st.lane_enters; st.travel_region; st.intersection), the place at which the intention of s14 is declared.

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway) that i lies on (st.on_way) other than a highway c lies on. 'one-way to the left': at least one lane (st.lane) lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction (st.lane_direction) to the left of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's being above p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is not nearness.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, occupies at the judged observation, or occupied at the previous one, a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); s displays a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state) at the judged observation; and at the previous observation the subject's footprint overlapped neither i nor a crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of). The duty does not apply where paragraph (c) permits the movement (spans s7 to s15, the words NRS_484B_307_8a_o3 reads as its conditions): the subject has halted at the place of the stop on this approach (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance; the place, zone p.stop_point_tolerance and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1: the search runs back from the judged observation to the approach start on c or to the subject's previous entry into i from c), and either (right) c is a lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction, int.right_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every highway i lies on other than one c lies on is two-directional (no median or divider lies on it; two lanes on it with directions opposed within p.lane_opposed_direction_cos) or one-way to the right (every lane on it points to the right of c's direction by more than p.cross_direction_sin_min); or (left) c is a lane of ordinal 1, the subject's footprint overlaps a one-way roadway, int.left_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every such highway is one-way to the left. The permission is read whether the subject's footprint now overlaps the crosswalk marking c's entrance or i itself. The duty also does not apply where NRS_484B_307_8d (paragraph (d), s5) applies to the subject.
obligation: At the judged observation the subject's footprint overlaps neither i nor a crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (rel.occupies): having stopped, or still short of the place, it remains short of them while the steady red alone is displayed; once s displays another state (the green shown) the duty no longer applies.

narrowings.why: 'remain stopped or standing' is read at the place the stop was due: the subject leaves the stop when its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking its carrier's entrance or the intersection while the steady red alone is displayed. A movement short of them, such as closing up behind a vehicle ahead before reaching the place or a creep within the stop-point zone, is not read as leaving the stop: the stop the words require is the one at the place.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line of lane c (ordinal 2 of 3), which enters i and is governed by head s displaying circular_red alone; int.right_turn is not declared; 5 s later it moves off and its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking c's entrance while s still displays circular_red alone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at the line under circular_red alone and stays short of the crosswalk until s displays circular_green; it then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone throughout the car's approach and entry.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions s governs: whether the car faces s is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts with its body 1 m short of the stop line in the rightmost lane (ordinal 3 of 3), int.right_turn is declared for it at i, and the cross street is undivided with lanes in both directions; it moves off and its footprint comes to overlap the crosswalk marking c's entrance under circular_red alone: paragraph (c)'s permission holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the cross street is one-way and every lane on it points to the car's left: the permission does not hold, and leaving the stop under the red violates.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1, but the car halted 15 m short of the line behind a queue and, when the queue cleared, rolled to the line and into the crosswalk without halting at the place: the halt the permission refers to did not occur.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_20_060_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.lane_opposed_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) off exactly opposed at which the designated directions of two mapped lanes of one way count as opposite directions of travel: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way
param_proposals.source: map lane-direction tolerance, matching the catalogue's tolerance for opposed vehicle headings (p.oncoming_heading_cos)

param_proposals.name: p.cross_direction_sin_min
param_proposals.convention: sine of the smallest angle (thirty degrees) by which a way's designated direction lies to one side of an approach's designated direction for that way's traffic to count as flowing to that side: the legs of a junction meet at larger angles, and map direction noise is far smaller
param_proposals.source: intersection design guidance limiting the skew of junction legs

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) On a day on which the school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', recognized when b comes to be behind a after b was ahead with headings aligned within same_dir_cos. 'overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction' is that act with a the subject and b any other road user of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the admitted aggregate of 'vehicle', 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'); the concept's aligned headings carry 'in the same direction'. The concept 'says nothing ... of whether b moves', so 'traveling' is carried beside it: b's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, so a pass of a vehicle at rest throughout is not this duty. b is quantified in the rule, not a binder. The concept reads kin.position, kin.heading and rel.longitudinal_overlap ('Where the positions of a and b are unobserved, it is unknown'); its call is expanded, so those atoms count as the rule's.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and the school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-060: 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are those categories; the area designated as either is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region); the pass is made in it where, while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', read only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position'. 'designated' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r.

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend' and prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'; env.civil_time is the primitive's own input.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). For each other road user b of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same(b, subject) excluded), the pass of b is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b; window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos), recognized at the observation at which it holds; it is under way from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction within p.overtake_same_direction_cos) up to the recognition. The duty applies to that pass where b's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, and where, at some observation while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, and, for that z and r, none of the exceptions holds at every observation while the pass is under way: (a) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (b) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (c) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (d) no beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. With no other vehicle in the scene the duty is met.
obligation: For every such b, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos does not hold at the judged observation: a recognized pass of a travelling vehicle in the zone violates the duty. Where the window behind is truncated, or the overlap of the two bodies' projections (rel.longitudinal_overlap) or the positions of the subject or b are unobserved, the pass and its occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' and 'overtake' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence.

under_way.words: from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the moving subject with headings aligned, up to the recognition
under_way.justification: drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)', where 'b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)'. The pass is under way from that observation to the recognition, while the subject moves (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and closes on b; the subject's motion and the relations it changes tell an observation inside the pass from one before it began, where the subject occupied the same lane, so no region alone could.

segmentation.text: Except if required by an emergency
or as otherwise authorized by subsection 3
[(3) appended below],
a person shall not drive a vehicle
on a controlled-access highway:
Upon any portion of the highway that lies outside of a marked traffic lane or marked entrance or exit lane.
A person driving a vehicle described in
paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210
[list appended below]
may drive that vehicle on a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.
The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to:
(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;
(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;
(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;
(d) A tow car;
(e) A coroner vehicle;
or (f) A public transit motor bus,
that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: An emergency requiring the movement is not observable; it is read through the conduct that shows it: the subject's hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard, "both indicators flashing together", as a disabled or imperilled vehicle shows), or the subject an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") showing a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp, "a warning lamp lit"). ru.emergency_vehicle is "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle — the class alone is not responding": the class is read only together with its lit warning lamp, and an unobserved lamp leaves the exception unknown.

Authorization by subsection 3 is the permission subsection 3 states (spans e7, e10, e12-e18): a shoulder-use permission posted by a dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", of code shoulder_use_permitted; this span joins that permission to the duty as an exception.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway". "drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed at or below a tolerance the caller sets") not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060, "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only"): st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes", whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, which lists the controlled-access lane).

A portion of the highway outside a marked traffic lane or entrance or exit lane: a st.shoulder ("the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic") or a st.median_or_divider ("physical barrier or dividing section between roadways") whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or no st.lane ("a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") overlapped at all while the subject is on the controlled-access highway. Lanes include the entrance and exit lanes of st.controlled_access. st.lane is not a lateral position within a lane: membership is read from occupancy.
The person driving a vehicle of the classes listed (e12-e17): the subject vehicle, admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; which vehicles are described is read from the list.

On a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder whose paved attribute holds while it occupies the st.controlled_access region. Lawfully placed signage allowing that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governing that shoulder (dev.governs lists the shoulder among the regions a device governs), whose structured conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user", the class condition included). A sign is not a road feature: the permission is the sign's, read as it is posted.

"Authorized emergency vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law"; the words borrowed through the reference e8 list it among the vehicles NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;" following it. The run's reading classifies every road-user class under this id as unresolved and none as included, so the leaf is unknown for every road user and never decides the exception: the gap on this span records that membership is not decidable. ru.emergency_vehicle ("vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") is the nearest class atom; it is not the legal permission the definition states, and an admitted aggregate is never replaced by a class atom.

"(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;": a vehicle permitted to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law"; the permit is the legal basis of that membership, which the run's reading classifies. Membership is undecidable under the current reading for the reason the gap on e12 states, which this span shares. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind incident_management; it is "not a stand-in for an emergency vehicle", and none is read from it. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(d) A tow car;": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, "a motor vehicle which has been altered or designed and equipped for and exclusively used in the business of towing vehicles by means of a crane, hoist, tow bar, towline or dolly, or is otherwise exclusively used to render assistance to other vehicles". The gate's evidence (iteration 2: aggregate_unresolved for DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car on a transit bus; iteration 3: no literal variant of the subject's aggregate leaves exercised) shows the run's reading decides no road user a member, so the gap on this span records it. ru.official_vehicle of kind tow ("a vehicle in official or contracted road service") is the nearest class atom and is narrower than the definition; it does not replace the aggregate. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(e) A coroner vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", kind coroner; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"or (f) A public transit motor bus,": the words name a road-user class that has its own atom, ru.transit_bus, "bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display" (a bus, ru.bus, being a "motor vehicle designed to carry many passengers": the "motor bus" of the words). ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which the applicable definitions ... permit its own class atom — that class's own atom". The defined word "bus" (DEF-NRS-484A-030) includes every such vehicle: "a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision ... designed for carrying more than 10 passengers and used for the transportation of persons, or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation"; its exclusion "other than a taxicab" is already made by the contract. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

Being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway: the listed vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway it is on; where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder: a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governs (dev.governs) that shoulder and its conditions hold for the vehicle (prim.conditions_hold). st.on_way is not nearness: the shoulder belongs to the way by the relation. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

compositions.quote: (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;
compositions.why: The reference borrows only the list of vehicle classes NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth to name which vehicles subsection 3 permits on a signed paved shoulder; no rule of NRS 484B.210 needs to apply, hold or be complied with for this duty or its exception, and the list's words are appended in this line and carried by its own elements.

residues.why: Introduces the list of NRS 484B.210(4) as appended; the exemption from the passing rule of NRS 484B.210(1)(c)(1) it states is that section's, not this duty's, and is not read here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle in motion (drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold) whose footprint overlaps a controlled-access highway ca (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access). Exception (emergency): the duty does not apply where the subject's hazard lamps flash (sig.hazard) or the subject is an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle) with a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp).
obligation: The subject's footprint overlaps no st.median_or_divider; overlaps no st.shoulder other than an authorized one; and overlaps some st.lane unless every shoulder, median or divider it overlaps is an authorized shoulder (the controlled-access and highway regions it overlaps are the highway itself, not a portion outside a lane). A shoulder s is authorized (subsection 3) where the subject is a listed vehicle — a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, a ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management or coroner, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-280::tow_car, or a ru.transit_bus — and s is paved, lies on the highway the subject is on (st.on_way, st.highway), and is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold). The node is not coded while the gaps on e12 and e15 stand: under the run's reading neither listed aggregate decides any road user a member.

narrowings.why: "a person shall not drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle in motion is driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
An emergency is read through the conduct that shows it: hazard lamps flashing, or an emergency vehicle showing a lit warning lamp.

"marked" lanes are read from the mapped lane regions; the portions outside them are read as shoulders, medians and dividers, and any footprint position on the controlled-access highway that overlaps no lane.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.

segmentation.text: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway shall, except:
(a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed
commensurate with the speed of
any nearby traffic;
(b) When preparing to turn left;
or
(c) When doing so would not be safe,
ride as near to the right side of the roadway
as practicable,
exercising due care
when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.

For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation:
(a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway.
(b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded into classes; 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading), not as a role atom, which the aggregate's 'not a stand-in for' clause excludes.

'upon a roadway': st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; rel.occupies anchors the subject ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'upon a roadway shall, except:' (NRS_484B_777_1_o2). 'shall, except:' introduces the exceptions of this roadway duty. The words of exception (b) name no place for the left turn; a left turn off a roadway is made where it meets another way, so the declared intention is read at every kind of region where that happens: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') and st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'), the latter covering every alley, driveway and private road entrance.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'), one ru.aggregate atom. 'any nearby traffic' is every road user of that aggregate, other than the subject, whose body gap to the subject (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is within the nearby reach, whatever its direction of travel; where none is nearby the comparison holds vacuously ('any'), the subject then holding back no traffic. surface_gap is the body gap itself, not a centre distance.

The right side of the roadway is its right edge: st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway', lying on the same highway (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind) as the roadway the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.roadway). Nearness is the gap between the subject's body and that edge: prim.region_lateral_offset is 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', negative for an edge on the right, less half the subject's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'); st.region_geometry carries the edge's outline the primitive reads, and its 'not a stand-in for occupancy' clause does not apply, occupancy being read by rel.occupies. Same family of atoms as the index's 'drive to the extreme right side of the highway' (NRS_484B_627_1a), here on the roadway's edge.

Things that impede access to the right side: 'fixed or moving objects', 'animals' and 'surface hazards' are st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind in {debris, excavation, hose, barrier, stalled_vehicle_wreckage, sidewalk_fixture, mail_drop_box, other}' (an animal that is not ridden or herded is such an object, kind other); 'parked or moving vehicles', 'bicycles' and 'pedestrians' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle and DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, whatever their motion. Impeding access is the thing lying in the rider's way on its right side: for an object, ahead of the subject along the designated direction of the roadway it occupies within the reach (prim.region_offset_along, 'the signed distance (m) from a road user's reference point to a structure region ... measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)', from zero to the reach) and at or to the right of the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset at or below zero), its outline being st.region_geometry; for a road user, the body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the reach, ahead and at or to the right of the subject (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame'). Neither atom is used for a clearance it excludes: surface_gap is the body gap itself; bearing is a direction only.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed commensurate with the speed of nearby traffic
operationalizations.convention: Traveling is the subject's speed (kin.speed) above the source's speed resolution (p.halt_speed_tolerance). The subject's speed is commensurate with the nearby traffic (s4b: traffic road users within p.nearby_traffic_reach, two seconds of headway at urban speed) where each such road user's speed exceeds the subject's by no more than p.commensurate_speed_margin, a speed differential within one traffic stream; the bound moves with both measured speeds.

operationalizations.standard: when doing so would not be safe
operationalizations.convention: Not safe is read through the two conditions subsection 2 names: (a) an object, vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach (s13), the distance within which a rider must steer around it; (b) the lane the subject occupies narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width (s14), the wide-outside-lane width of bicycle facility guidance below which a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot share a lane side by side.

operationalizations.standard: as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable
operationalizations.convention: As near as practicable is a gap between the subject's body and the roadway's right edge of at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap: a bicyclist's shy distance from a curb or edge plus the sway of its operating space and the source's position error (AASHTO bicycle operating space).

operationalizations.standard: the conditions under which it is not safe ... include, without limitation
operationalizations.convention: The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions and road users of the named aggregates on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach, and a lane narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width.

operationalizations.standard: a lane too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane
operationalizations.convention: The lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane) has a width (st.lane_width, 'width of a lane at a point') below p.shared_lane_min_width: 14 ft, the lane width below which bicycle facility guidance (AASHTO, MUTCD shared-lane guidance) holds that a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot travel safely side by side within one lane; the bicycle and the vehicle are the design road users the width stands for, not road users present in the scene.

applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate and its footprint overlaps a roadway at the observation, and none of the exceptions holds there: (a) the subject is traveling (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), complies with NRS_484B_785_1a (its lawful speed: the accepted record that an electric scooter on a roadway or bicycle lane or path travels at no more than its stated speed; a subject it does not engage complies), and every road user of the traffic aggregate other than the subject whose body gap to it is within p.nearby_traffic_reach has a speed no greater than the subject's plus p.commensurate_speed_margin (vacuously true where no such road user is nearby); (b) for some intersection or driveway/alley entrance r, the source's declaration current at the observation states int.left_turn for the subject at r; (c) not safe: some obstruction o lies ahead of the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach along the designated direction of a roadway the subject occupies (prim.region_offset_along from zero to the reach) with a lateral offset from the subject at or below zero (on its right or overlapping its line), or some road user of the vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian aggregate other than the subject has a body gap to the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach and a bearing whose longitudinal component is positive and lateral component at or below zero, or the subject occupies a lane whose width is below p.shared_lane_min_width.
obligation: At the observation the subject rides as near the right side of the roadway as practicable: with r a roadway the subject occupies, for some road edge e lying on a highway on which r lies, with e's lateral offset from the subject negative (on its right), the magnitude of that offset less half the subject's width (kin.extent) is at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap. Where no road edge on a highway of r lies on the subject's right in the scene, or the offset is unobserved, the verdict is unknown (definedWhen), never violated.

narrowings.why: 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion on the roadway, whoever controls it.

The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions, and road users of the vehicle, bicycle and pedestrian aggregates, in the rider's way on its right, and a lane narrower than the shared-lane width; other unsafe conditions, among them road users of no named aggregate (electric bicycles and electric scooters, which the vehicle and bicycle definitions leave out), are not read.
The right side is read relative to the subject's heading (the primitive's frame), and the edge is a mapped road edge on a highway the occupied roadway lies on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides at 5 m/s on a roadway whose outside lane is 5.0 m wide, its body 2.5 m from the right road edge; a car of the vehicle and traffic aggregates travels the same way at 13 m/s with a body gap of 20 m behind it; no obstruction or other road user is on its right, no intersection or driveway entrance is in the scene, so no left turn is declared.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the bicycle rides with its body 0.6 m from the right road edge.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk, its footprint overlapping no roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source maps regions without their outlines, so the road edge's lateral offset from the bicycle is unobserved.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides alone at 5 m/s in the middle of a 5.0 m outside lane; no other road user is in the scene, so exception (a) holds vacuously: the duty binds the subject alone and is decided.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the outside lane is 3.5 m wide, below the shared-lane width (exception (c), s14).

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a parked car of the vehicle aggregate stands 10 m ahead of the bicycle on its right, at the curb (exception (c), s13).

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but an intersection lies ahead and the source declares int.left_turn for the bicycle at it (exception (b)).

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides at 8 m/s, above the speed NRS_484B_785_1a allows it, 2.5 m from the right edge of a 5.0 m lane; a car travels the same way at 9 m/s 20 m behind it: its speed is commensurate but not lawful, so exception (a) fails.
